newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Czech Prime Minister visits Euro-defence body.
newsitem.headline: Czech Prime Minister visits Euro-defence body.

text.p: The prime minister of the Czech Republic, a country leading the field to join the west's democratic institutions, began a visit to Brussels on Tuesday aimed at strengthening his country's case for swift admission.
Vaclav Klaus told reporters he had had "very fruitful and friendly talks" with Jose Cutileiro, the secretary-general of the European Union's emerging defence body, the Western European Union (WEU).

Later in the day, Klaus will meet EU Commission President Jacques Santer and stress that his country's reform process has left it with one of the most successful economies of the former communist states of central and eastern Europe.
The Czech Republic, strongly supported by France, is lobbying hard to be in the first wave of new democracies to join the EU, the WEU and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).

NATO is set to invite new members to join the military alliance at a special summit in Madrid next July. EU membership will not take place until after the turn of the century, but Prague is keen to begin negotiations.

Those negotiations will not start until after a review by existing member governments of the EU's founding treaties this summer which may also bring the WEU into a closer permanent relationship with the European Union.
